rows.what: Read the 202 Arienzo processetti pages, and sweep the collection for the other surnames
rows.note:
**Row 62 found the seam; this row works it.** FamilySearch collection **`2043630`** holds **202 distinct Arienzo pages** naming a Falco, 1891–1910, and their certified extracts quote Arienzo civil acts from years Antenati does not hold. **One pass on one surname recovered seventeen.**

**Three jobs, in order.**

**1. Read the images.** Every extract in `notes/arienzo-1866-1890-via-processetti.md` carries its ark. **A machine transcription is a candidate and nothing more** — the OCR renders Arienzo as «Chienno», «Criengo» and «Artento» on the same pages. Nothing enters a household until the image is read. Start with the three that touch **Matteo Falco × Alessandra Crisci**, whose nine children have no documents at all: `3:1:3QS7-897N-5R1` (Filomena, 1872), `3:1:3QS7-897N-16SB` (Vincenza, 1874), `3:1:3QS7-897N-P3N5` (Giuseppe & Nicoletta Nuzzo, 1887).

**2. Sweep the other surnames.** Only `q.text=Falco` has been run. **Crisci, Guida, Arricale, Annecchino, Carfora, Cimmino, Morgillo, Zampiello, Rivetti, Cioffi** have not.

**3. Sweep the wording, not the name** — `q.text=Estratto` enumerates every processetto in the collection whoever it belongs to, which is how the 1866–1890 acts get counted rather than sampled.

**The prize.** Rows 39 and 40 want the deaths of **Giuseppe Falco of Antonia di Guida** and **Vincenzo Falco of Andreana Crisci**, both after 1865 and both unfound. A grandchild marrying in the 1890s would have had to produce exactly those extracts.

**FIRST RESULTS, 16 September.** A second sweep on `q.text=Carfora` brings the corpus to **347 distinct Arienzo pages**, and three things fell out of it:

**A FOURTH child of MATTEO FALCO × ALESSANDRA CRISCI.** The 1908 proclamation names «*FERRARA AGNESE, 25, figlia di **GIOVANNI**, 60, colono, e figlia di **MARIA FALCO**, contadina, residente in Arienzo*» — and the tree holds **Giovanni Ferrara married to Maria Falco (Ferrara)**, daughter of Matteo and Alessandra, with `records: 0` against both. **Both alive at Arienzo in 1908, and a granddaughter the tree does not have.**

**THE CORSO CAUDINO HOUSEHOLD CLOSES ON ITSELF.** Vincenzo Falco × Angela Pellone, of Corso Caudino 80 — a birth in 1880, his death in 1889 — now has a daughter: «*Falco **PASQUALINA**, 21, **figlia del fu VINCENZO** … e di **PELLONE ANGELA***», marrying Crisci Raffaele in 1899. **Three acts, one household, two separate sweeps.**

**A THIRD HOUSE NUMBER ON STRADA CAMELLARA.** A 1906 supplement quotes an Arienzo birth act of about 1879: «*è comparso **PASQUALE FALCO**, contadino, di anni trentanove … nella casa posta in **VIA CUMELLARA AL NUMERO UNDICI**, da **MARIA AMALIA GUIDA***». That is this archive's own household, and the age agrees with his death act — **but he dies at number FIVE**, and the Morgillo are at **number NINE** in 1881. **Three numbers where the archive had one, and no reason yet to think they are stable.**

**All of it is still machine transcription. The images are unread.**

rows.what: Read the Arienzo «Diversi» register — the deaths that happened somewhere else
rows.note:
**A WHOLE SERIES THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER OPENED, found on 17 September while looking for something else.** Its title page: «*Atti per le nascite avvenuti in un viaggio di mare, Per le Ricognizioni, Adozioni, **PERSONE DEFUNTE E FUORI DEL PROPRIO DOMICILIO**, e Morti-Nati*».

**When an Arienzo person died elsewhere, the comune where they died drew the act and sent a certified copy to Arienzo, which copied it in whole** — age, trade, street, both parents, whether they were dead, and the surviving children with their ages. **So a death that is not in the Arienzo death register may be here, because the person did not die at Arienzo.**

**That is exactly the shape of rows 39 and 40.** GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida is alive in November 1849 and in no volume since; ANTONIA DI GUIDA is alive in February 1845 and in none either. **Read 1849 onward first.**

**The series is small.** Forty years — 1703, 1812–1813, 1820, 1822–1835, 1837–1840, 1842–1850, 1853, 1855–1860, 1864–1865 — at **one to eight images each**, so the whole thing is about the size of a single year of deaths.

**THE ARK ARITHMETIC IS NOT LINEAR AND MUST NOT BE GUESSED.** `an_ua14056`–`14062` run 1835, 1837, 1839, 1840, 1846, 1848, 1849 — ascending with gaps — but `an_ua14071` is **1825** and `an_ua14095` is **1848**, so at least two sub-series are interleaved in the range. **Probe each ark and read the breadcrumb.** Antenati rate-limits hard: seven probes 0.8 s apart earned a 403 on the eighth.

**1825 is read** (`an_ua14071`, two acts): a colono who died at a masseria in the **Nola** district, and a woman of fifty-five who died in the **Real Stabilimento delle Donne Matte at Aversa** with her parents left blank. **Method, arks and both transcriptions: `notes/arienzo-diversi-series.md`.**

---

**17 SEPTEMBER — THE MAP IS COMPLETE AND THE READING HAS STARTED.**

**All 45 volumes located, 1812–1865, ark by year, in five requests** — and **the table published here yesterday was wrong**. It listed `an_ua14056`–`14062` as Diversi, from probing arks and reading the breadcrumb year; **those arks are a different series** and the assumption was mine. **Do not probe arks.** `/search-registry/?localita=Arienzo&tipologia=Diversi` renders `<li class="search-item" data-id="NNNNN">` with `Registro: YYYY` beside it — ten a page, `&s_page=N` to continue. (`&anno=YYYY` breaks the page entirely.) The real block is **`an_ua14064`–`14106`, plus `an_ua57637`–`57638` for 1813.**

**A METHOD TRAP, FOUND THE HARD WAY.** Each act is headed «*Atto di morte fuori domicilio di [NAME]*» and in 1849–1850 that heading is the perfect sweep band. **From 1856 the clerk leaves the printed heading blank and writes only the body**, so the heading sweep reported «no acts» for a volume holding five. **Sweep `--band 0.06 0.30 --half LR`.** The reading of **1855 as empty is void** and must be redone.

**READ SO FAR.** **1849** — three acts, all «morte fuori domicilio», **no Falco**. **1850** — «*ESTRATTO DI MORTE*» from the **Comune di AIROLA**: «*è morto nella strada Mercato **NICOLA D'ADDIO**, **nato in ARIENZO**, di anni ventisei, Bracciale, domiciliato in Airola **DI PASSAGGIO**, figlio di **PIETRO**, Bracciale, domiciliato in **Arienzo**, e fu **FLAVIA TANOLLA***». **Exactly the record this series exists for** — a man of Arienzo who died in the next town and is invisible to every Arienzo death sweep. **1853** — two deaths transmitted from **NAPLES**, one from the Sezione Montecalvario, plus local acts for Carmela de Roggio and Antonio Rivetti. **1856, 1857** — acts present, bodies unread.

**STILL TO READ: 1855, 1858–1865, the bodies of 1853/1856/1857, and the whole of 1812–1848.** Neither GIUSEPPE FALCO nor ANTONIA DI GUIDA has appeared yet, and **nothing about rows 39 and 40 may be concluded until the series is finished.**

---

**17 SEPTEMBER, SECOND PASS — AND THE SERIES IS NOT WHAT ITS NAME SAYS.**

**`localita=Arienzo` RETURNS VOLUMES FROM SEVERAL COMUNI.** More than one comune in this district has «Arienzo» in its name, and the holdings list matches all of them. Read from the manuscripts: `an_ua14064` and `14069` and `14071` are «*Comune di **CORPO D'ARIENZO***»; **`an_ua57637` and `57638` (1813) are «*Comune di SAN FELICE D'ARIENZO*»**; **`an_ua14068` (1824) is «*Comune di SAN CASALE DI ARIENZO*»**. **The printed title page gives the CIRCONDARIO — Arienzo — at the top, and that is the district, not the town.** The comune is the line below it. **A sweep that reads the top of the page will call every volume Arienzo and be wrong about a third of them**, and this archive has a standing refusal to claim the San Felice Falco as kin. **Read the comune before attributing anything.**

**READ SO FAR — no Falco, no di Guida, anywhere.** **1812** two death acts, both **CRISCI**, natives of Arienzo: **MARCO CRISCI** received from the Sindaco of **ACERRA**, and a second received from **MONTESARCHIO**. **1820** one stillbirth. **1822, 1823, 1824 (`14069`), 1825 (`14070`)** — **no acts at all**, title page and ministerial certificate only. **1824 (`14068`, San Casale)** one act. **1825 (`14071`)** the two already published. **1849** three acts. **1850** Nicola d'Addio, died at **Airola**. **1853** two deaths from **Naples**.

**STILL TO READ: `an_ua14072`–`14095` — twenty-four volumes, 1826 to 1848, about 100 images — then 1855, 1858, 1859, 1860, 1864, 1865, and the bodies of 1853, 1856 and 1857.** Roughly half the series. **Nothing about rows 39 and 40 may be concluded until it is finished.**

---

**FINISHED 20 September 2026 — 45 volumes, 1812 to 1865, and there is no Falco in any of them.**

**Every act from 1845 to 1865 has been read and its dead named** — which is the window rows 39 and 40 need, since **Antonia di Guida is alive on 2 February 1845** and **Giuseppe Falco on 26 November 1849**. **Neither died away from Arienzo in a way this register recorded.** Three acts in the whole series remain unnamed — two in 1835, one in 1839, one in 1840 — and all are **before 1845**, so none can be either of them.

**What the series turned out to be.** About **thirty-five deaths away from home** for Corpo d'Arienzo, mapping where an Arienzo labourer went and did not come back from: the **Ospedale degli Incurabili** at Naples (5), **Sant'Agostino degli Scalzi** at Aversa (3), the **Real Stabilimento de' Matti** and its women's side at Aversa (6), **Acerra** (3), **Caserta** (2), **Airola** (2), a masseria in the **Nola** district, **Montesarchio**, **Santa Maria Maggiore**, the **Ospedale della Trinità**, and — once — **LIPARI**.

**The four that are worth a page of their own:**

- **PASQUALE PORRINO**, 52, married, a labourer born at Arienzo, dead **31 October 1864 in the hospital of the DOMICILIATI COATTI on LIPARI** — internal exile, three years after Unification.
- **CARLO BALLETTA**, soldier of the **1° Reggimento Dragoni**, dead in the **Ospedale della Trinità** on 3 March 1855; his colonel wrote asking the sindaco to tell the family to send someone for **one ducat and thirty-five grana**, the proceeds of his kit.
- **ANGELO IMBIMBO**, 60, dead in the **Aversa madhouse** on 30 November 1855 — and the 1845 volume has **FRANCESCO IMBIMBO, «figlio d'ANGELO»**, dead in the **same asylum** on 4 November 1844. **Father and son, eleven years apart.**
- **PELLEGRINO MORGILLO**, 26, «*vedovo di MARIANTONIA D'ADDIO*», dead at Aversa in 1828 — a year after the Giudicato Regio's letter about his wife's body found buried in a wood.

**Two surnames are left deliberately unread**, both flagged rather than guessed: the **RI[?]ETTI** of January 1845 («*figlia del fu MATTEO*») and the **[T/D]IGLI** of December 1855. **Neither is Falco.** Both are worth settling, because Rivetti and Diglio are families this archive holds.

**Method, every volume, every act and every ark: `notes/arienzo-diversi-series.md`.**

rows.what: WO 32/22147 — a British Army investigation into a killing at Arienzo, March 1945
rows.note:
**The only record in the whole of the UK National Archives that touches this family's town.** «*Special Investigation Branch investigation: alleged murder of **Herron FG, Private, 1583838, Argyle and Sutherland Highlanders**, **by two Italian civilians at ARIENZO, Italy, 11 March 1945***». 1–31 March 1945, **open** since 25 August 2017, held at **Kew**, **not digitised**.

**IT IS A LEAD ABOUT ARIENZO, NOT ABOUT THE FALCO, and it is recorded as that.** No Falco is named in the catalogue description and none may be assumed. What makes it worth ordering is that **this archive holds almost nothing from Arienzo in the 1940s** — the civil registers stop at 1865, the processetti at 1865, and the Australian records begin in 1964. A military police file names its accused and its witnesses, and its witnesses would be townspeople.

**It needs a person.** Kew will copy it on request, or it can be read in the reading room. **That is why this row is blocked rather than next.**

rows.what: Order the Arienzo 1845 processetto and settle whether Crescenzo Falco's father-in-law is the Gennaro Morgillo who died on 4 August 1843
rows.note:
**The marriage is act 3 of 2 February 1845, Arienzo — `an_ua14249` img4R.** Its *processetto* must contain a death certificate for **GENNARO MORGILLO**, because the bride is described as an orphan of both parents, and a Neapolitan marriage dossier of this date proves that with the civil death act itself. **That certificate will quote an act number.** If it is **33 of 1843**, the man who died a widower on strada Camellara on 4 August 1843 — son of Angelo Morgillo, colono of the Monticello de' Cappuccini — is Crescenzo Falco's father-in-law, and the Falco and the Morgillo of the hill are joined by a document instead of by four agreeing details.

**It would also read a surname this archive cannot.** The 1843 act calls his wife «Felicia S___»; the archive published «Sompone» and the 1845 marriage gives «SANSONE». At the leaf's full resolution — 1,622 pixels across a half page, which is where this filming stops — the word will not separate. **The processetto would carry her death act too.**

**And it is the same bundle that would answer row 40's other question**, since a 1845 dossier for an Arienzo bride quotes the birth act as well: Angela Maria Morgillo is twenty-three in February 1845, so born about 1822, in a birth register this archive has not read.

---

## ANSWERED — 21 September 2026. IT IS ACT 33, AND NOTHING HAD TO BE ORDERED.

**This row opens with the word «Order». It was the second row in one day to be wrong about that.** The Arienzo *processetti* for 1845 are **`an_ua14190`, 432 images**, free on Antenati; **bundle 3 is images 27–39**; and it took four ark probes and two contact sheets to get there. See row 77 for the same lesson arriving first.

### The question this row was raised to ask

> *«If it is **33 of 1843**, the man who died a widower on strada Camellara on 4 August 1843 … is Crescenzo Falco's father-in-law.»*

**«MUNICIPALITÀ DI ARIENZO — Estratto di Morte del 1843 — Num. d'ordine TRENTATRE»**, issued «*per uso di matrimonio*» on **22 November 1844**, **filed twice** in the bundle at images 31 and 32. **PROVED.** The Falco of strada Camellara and the Morgillo of the Monticello de' Cappuccini are joined by a document.

### The second question, and it was already answered elsewhere

This row wanted the processetto to read a surname the 1843 filming cannot resolve. **It does read it — «*vedovo di FELICIA SANSONE*» — but the better witness is the bride's own birth act**, which the dossier also named: **Arienzo, Nati 1822, act 66**, where the 1822 clerk splits the word at the syllable, «*MARIA FELICE **SAN=/SONE***». **Three documents in three hands.** «Sompone» is finished.

### The third question, thrown in

> *«a 1845 dossier for an Arienzo bride quotes the birth act as well: Angela Maria Morgillo is twenty-three in February 1845, so born about 1822.»*

**Born 2 August 1822, act 66, at seventeen hours, in her father's house on strada VALLONE** — read from the register, not from the dossier's copy. **Which makes her twenty-TWO when she married**, and the dossier's copy of the promise says «*ventidue*» where the register's own act 3 says «*ventitre*». *Two copies of one act, one year apart on the same woman.*

### What came out that nobody asked for

**GIUSEPPE FALCO WAS A COLONO**, and both he and **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** are unmarked — alive — on 2 February 1845, in an act that marks the bride's parents dead in the next sentence. **The banns were posted on Sunday 24 November 1844**, ten weeks before the wedding. **Angelo Morgillo had a wife**, «*MARIA G———*», named in the death extract and in the register act, and her surname will not resolve.

**And the register row for act 33 was wrong in four fields at once** — the date, the first declarant's age, the second declarant's surname, and the wife's. All four came from the sweep that found the act. **See the corrections page.**

rows.what: Reconcile the research log — it was showing 40 of the archive's 87 working files, and the other 47 had no row against them
rows.note:
**The research log had been generated by a script that never wrote the key the work list points at.** `tools/build_researchlog.py` produced rows without a `key` column while `checkcovers.py` resolves every «covers: log:NAME» against exactly that column. **So the file on disk carried keys that nothing could have put there, and the moment it was regenerated all thirty coverage links went blank and the build refused.** The generator is fixed; the key is the filename stem, lowercased, which is how the committed file had always spelt it.

**What the fix exposed is larger than the fix.** The log held **40 rows. There are 87 files in `notes/`.** Forty-seven of this archive's own working files — the death of Matteo Falco in 1802, the parish marriage indexes, the processetti mining, every FindMyPast harvest, the Zampiello of Arpaia — **had never reached the research-log page at all**, because the log had not been regenerated since they were written.

**Forty-four of them now count as outstanding and none of them has a row.** Most are not outstanding at all: they are finished findings, and the generator calls a file incomplete unless it contains the literal word COMPLETE, which only the per-volume sweeps use. **`unreconciled` is set to 44 deliberately** — the gate's own ratchet — **and the number is printed on every build so it cannot be forgotten.** The work is to walk the forty-four, attach each to the row that owns it or mark the file finished in its own words, and take the number down.

**It is the Mazza fault in a second place.** A generator quietly stopped writing a column a consumer keys on, and nothing refused until a gate was pointed at it.

## DONE, 20 September 2026 — and the backlog was never forty-four

**The account was measuring the wrong thing.** «Research files not finished» was pointed at `not complete`, and `complete` answers a different question: **was this REGISTER read end to end.** A FINDING file has no reason to contain the word COMPLETE, so all fifty-three of them — the death of Matteo Falco, the parish marriage indexes, every FindMyPast harvest, the Zampiello of Arpaia — **were being counted as outstanding work.** **Forty-four closed pieces of work sat in a backlog they never belonged in.**

**`build_researchlog.py` now writes `outstanding` separately**, and the definition is a real convention and not a guess: **a file is outstanding when it is a per-volume SWEEP that has not finished.** This archive names those `*-progress.md` — **thirty-four of the eighty-seven files** — and nothing else.

**The number fell from forty-four to one**, and the one was real: **the Arienzo civil marriage register for 1815, images 17 to 30, never opened** — about twelve marriages, half the year, in the densest kind of volume this archive reads. **That is now row 81.**

**`unreconciled` is 0.** The work list accounts for **26 of 26** outstanding items: twenty-three unfinished register sweeps and three towns whose processetti are unexamined. **The ratchet can only tighten from here.**

**The lesson is the one this whole day has been about.** The gate was right that something was uncounted; **it was the archive's own declaration that told it what to count, and the declaration was wrong.** A number that is too big is not a safe error — it hides the one item that matters inside forty-three that do not.

rows.what: Reconcile households.tsv against households.json, and make the gate check the evidence and not just the names
rows.note:
**This archive keeps the same facts twice** — `data/households.tsv` and `site/src/data/households.json` — and edits both by hand. `check_release.py` refuses when they disagree about **who is in which household**, keyed on «household, person, event, date». **It has never compared the evidence text**, and on 20 September 2026 **thirty-seven rows were found to disagree about what the document actually says.**

**Three of them mattered and are already fixed.** The TSV held «*Magdalenae **RIVETTA*** — READ FROM THE IMAGE 14 Sep 2026» while the JSON, which the site is built from, still said «**Pivera**» — an OCR guess this archive had disproved six days earlier against a control letter in the same pen. It also held the note that Clemente Falco's parish entry says 1855 where the civil act says 1853.

**The rest is drift and has to be walked.** A person can hold several rows under one date, so the mismatch cannot be resolved by a script without choosing between two readings — which is a judgement, not a merge. **Nothing here may be bulk-copied in either direction.**

**Then the gate.** Once the two files agree, `check_release.py` should compare the evidence as well as the names, so the next correction that stops halfway is refused instead of published. **The whole point of keeping the file twice is lost if only one copy is ever read.**

## DONE, 20 September 2026 — sixty rows, nine recoveries, and the gate now reads the evidence

**Sixty rows disagreed about what the document says**, not thirty-seven: the number had grown all day because this row's own verification work was going into the JSON and being mirrored only narrowly.

**Thirty-six were the JSON ahead of the TSV** — today's readings — and were mirrored forward **only where the JSON provably contains the TSV's own text**, tested by normalised substring, never by length.

**NINE WERE THE TSV HOLDING SOMETHING THE SITE HAD NEVER SHOWN.** Two of them were live over-claims: **GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA and GIUSEPPE MORGILLO were published as «so alive» on the «quondam» signal this archive disproved on 14 September.** The downgrade reached the TSV and stopped. **The archive stopped believing it six days before it stopped saying it.** The other seven: the identification of **the fourth Maria Falco**; that her household lasted at most a few years; **Suor Maria Maddalena Rivetti** as the third sign of a Rivetti house of standing; **why the 1841 machine-transcript row is deliberately left standing** beside the act it duplicates; the refusal that **Vigliotti and Vigliotta are not established as one family**; that Domenico Clemente Falco's margin is **where this archive's margin method came from**; and the *muratore* note on Filomena di Lucia's father.

**The two files now agree row for row, and `check_release.py` compares the EVIDENCE as well as the names** — on whitespace-flattened text, allowing several entries under one key, because a person legitimately appears twice under one date. **Verified by reintroducing the «Pivera» fault: the gate refuses it with exit 1.** It prints the warning it has to as well — **do not bulk-copy, the newer text is not always the longer one** — which is how three corrected readings were nearly destroyed this morning.

rows.what: sitemap.py and checkarchive.py disagree about where a noindex tag may be
rows.note:
**`sitemap.py` decides whether a page noindexes itself by reading its first 4,000 bytes.** `checkarchive.py` then refuses the build if the sitemap lists any page whose **whole file** contains such a tag. **So a noindex tag below the fold is invisible to the first and fatal to the second**, and the build fails with a message that points at the page rather than at the disagreement.

**That is exactly what happened on 20 September 2026**, twice, when a commit message quoting a robots tag was rendered into the body of `/changes`. The archive's own bug is fixed — `build_changes.py` escapes what it writes — **but the disagreement is still there for the next archive.**

**Both files are in `@daviddef/archive-kit`, which another session owns.** Reported, not patched. The fix is one line: have `sitemap.py` scan the whole file, or have both agree on the same window.

rows.what: Order the Arienzo 1860 processetto — it holds a generation of the Annecchino and a birth act for Mariantonia Carfora
rows.note:
**The marriage act of 21 January 1860 lists the eight documents it was built on**, and four of them are papers this archive does not have.

**Item 4 — «*Nell'atto di morte dell'AVO PATERNO dello stesso*».** The **paternal grandfather of SABBATINO ANNECCHINO**, that is the father of **CARMINE ANNECCHINO of Forchia**. **A whole generation, named in a document that was read aloud at Arienzo and filed.** This archive has never had a name for him.

**Item 5** is **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA's birth act** — twenty-nine in January 1860, born at Arienzo about 1831, in a birth register nobody here has read. **Item 7** is **PASQUA MORGILLO's death act**, which dates the end of a Carfora–Morgillo marriage at Arienzo. **Item 6** is the **bride's father's consent** — this row called him «**VALERIO CARFORA**», and the forename was wrong; he is **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, and the consent paper is what proved it — and it will be signed or marked — **the only sample of him this archive could ever have.**

**Where it is.** Arienzo *processetti*, 1860, in the Antenati series this archive has surveyed but barely opened — **one bundle read out of three hundred and twenty**. Work-list rows 22 and 69 own the series; this row owns the year.

**Why this year before the others.** It is the only bundle this archive can name a specific missing generation inside.

---

## READ — 21 September 2026. IT WAS NEVER BLOCKED.

**This row said «order the processetto», and the bundle was on Antenati the whole time, free.** The Arienzo *processetti* for 1860 are **`an_ua14207`, 479 images**, and the archive's own holdings table already recorded that Arienzo has **63 processetti volumes covering 1809–1865** — it had the count and not the arks. **The arks run `an_ua14149` (1809) upward, one per year with a few years doubled**, and they were recovered in four probes.

**Finding the bundle.** Marriage act 3 of 1860 ⇒ bundle 3. Each dossier opens with the printed «*ESTRATTO della solenne promessa*» and runs about thirteen images: bundle 1 at image 2, bundle 2 at 15, **bundle 3 at images 25–42**, bundle 4 at 43. **Nothing had to be ordered and nothing had to be guessed.**

### What the four items held

**Item 4 — the paternal grandfather, and a generation past him.** Forchia, Morti **1826**, act **8**, **14 June 1826**: «*è morto nella sua propria casa **ANTONIO ANNECCHINO**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di anni **settantatre**, di professione **bracciale**, domiciliato ivi, figlio di **DOMENICO ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **ELISABETTA D'ONOFRIO defunta***». **Born about 1753 — and his own parents were dead before 1826, which puts DOMENICO ANNECCHINO in the 1710s or 1720s.** The dossier holds **two copies of this extract**, on images 30 and 31, word for word the same.

**Item 5 — Mariantonia Carfora's birth extract**, which gave the date (**30 December 1830**) and the act number (**142**). **The certified copy was not treated as the record**: the Arienzo birth register of 1830 was then opened at act 142 and read, and it is the original that this archive cites. See work-list row 63.

**Item 6 — the father's consent, and it demolished a published correction.** «*si è presentato **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, contadino di detto comune, il quale presta il suo pieno consenso alla sua figlia **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA***», Arienzo, **1 January 1860**, before the same Sindaco Sargenti who wrote the marriage act. **The forename this archive had published from the marriage act was wrong**, and this paper says so in a clear hand. He signed nothing — the act ends «*dovendo la parte apposta non sapere scrivere*». **There is no sample of him, and there never will be.**

**Item 7 — NOT FOUND.** «*Nell'atto di morte della madre della stessa*» — Pasqua Morgillo's death act — **is not in bundle 3**. Images 25 to 42 hold **four death extracts and every one is from Forchia**: Carmine Annecchino 1838, Rosa Ceglia 1852, and Antonio Annecchino 1826 twice. **The Arienzo paper the act says was read is not filed with the others.** This is recorded as a nil so nobody re-reads the bundle for it; where it went is not known.

### Two documents the row never asked for

**Item 1 — the groom's birth act.** Forchia, Nati **1825**, act **5**, **20 February 1825**: presented by **CARMINE ANNECCHINO, forty, bracciale, contrada detta li PRETI**, the mother «*ROSA CEGLIA sua moglie legittima, di anni trenta*», baptised the same day at **San Nicola**, the child named **SABATINO**.

**Items 2 and 3 — the groom's parents' deaths.** **CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, Forchia act 20, **8 August 1838**, fifty-two, colono of the **Masseria de' Preti**, son of Antonio Annecchino and Maria Guida. **ROSA CEGLIA**, Forchia act 4, **4 April 1852**, sixty-two, ***filatrice*, born at ARPAIA**, daughter of **Antonio Ceglia** and **Grazia Vitagliano** — **a surname that had never appeared in this archive in any file.**

**Four generations of Annecchino where there was one**, three new households, and a correction. **The lesson is the row's own first sentence.** It said «order», and the reason it said «order» is that the archive knew the series by a count in a survey table rather than by an ark, and a count cannot be opened. **Rows 22 and 69 own the rest of the series; 319 bundles are still shut.**

rows.what: Find Anna Falco's 1834 act, or retire her — the leaf cited for her holds another child
rows.note:
**Two rows on this site record an ANNA FALCO, eight days old, daughter of MICHELANGELO FALCO, dead on 7 March 1834**, both citing `an_ua14336` image 10 left. **Image 10 left is MARIA PORRINO** — eight days old, daughter of Angelo Porrino and Pasqua Rivetti, dead on **8** March 1834.

**Five leaves around it were opened on 20 September 2026 and none holds her.** The only act of 7 March on those leaves is Francesco Liparulo's. **And MICHELANGELO FALCO is a forename that appears nowhere else in this archive.**

**What to do.** The 1834 death register has its own **tavola alfabetica**; read it for FALCO, which is four images against ninety. If an Anna Falco of March 1834 is in it, the act number is there and this closes in an hour. **If she is not, she is a mis-indexed Maria Porrino and both rows are retired** — with the reasoning published, not deleted.

**Why it matters beyond one child.** She is entered twice, which means she has been counted twice in every total this archive publishes about the Falco of Arienzo.

## DONE, 20 September 2026 — and the index route was a dead end

**The 1834 death register has no *tavola* bound in**: its fifty-seven images end with the last act and a blank form. **The separate index volume, `an_ua14296`, is ONE IMAGE**, and that image covers **surnames A and C only** — the years on either side have six images and five. **The Arienzo death index for 1834 survives as a single leaf, and F is not on it.** That is a hole in the record, and it is published rather than left to be rediscovered.

**So she was found the other way.** A **contact-sheet sweep** of the volume's name lines — thirty-two tiles across sixteen leaves in one request — put her on **image 11 left**, and the leaf was then read at full resolution.

**ANNA FALCO IS REAL, AND ALMOST NOTHING ABOUT HER WAS RIGHT.** Act 16, **16 March 1834**, not the 7th. Eight days old, so born about 8 March. **Her mother is RAFFAELA FALCO** — a Falco married to a Falco, never recorded here — **not Mariantonia Vigliotta**, so she is not the child of the household she was filed under. Declared by **Giuseppe Carfora, forty** and **Tomaso Sposito, sixty**, both of **strada Camellara**.

**And one more age, for the series.** Tomaso Sposito is **forty-six in June 1824, fifty in April 1826, and sixty in March 1834**.

rows.what: Find where Don Giuseppe Cioffi's death act was actually read, or retire the reading
rows.note:
**The citation «`an_ua14329` img47L atto84» is impossible.** Arienzo Morti 1827 has **42 images and 68 acts**; neither the leaf nor the act exists, and three contact sheets across images 20–41 found no priest.

**The reading itself is detailed enough to have come from an act**: «*D. GIUSEPPE C—, d'anni **cinquantasei**, nato in Arienzo, di professione **SACERDOTE**, figlio di **ANDREA —**, possidente, e di **ORSOLA ZIMBARDO**, defunti*». It is not a guess and it is corroborated from the other end: his sister **CELIA CIOFFI**'s act of 3 June 1843 gives the same father, the same trade and the same mother.

**Where to look.** The date «4 December 1827» may itself be the error — try the **1826, 1828 and 1829** death registers, and the **death indexes** for those years, for a Giuseppe Cioffi aged about fifty-six, sacerdote. **If he is not in any of them, the reading came from a machine index and must be marked as one**, not retired: the parents are confirmed by a second act.

## FOUR YEARS EXCLUDED, 20 September 2026

**The death indexes for 1826, 1827, 1828 and 1829 were read** — `an_ua14288` to `an_ua14291`, nine leaves — **and the C block was opened in every one.** **There is no Giuseppe Cioffi, Crisci or Cossi described as SACERDOTE in any of the four years.** The only religious in the stretch is **Crisci Suor Maria Teresa**, a *monaca*, in 1827.

**So the year is wrong by more than two, or the reading never came from a death act.** The second is now the likelier, and the same four indexes showed why: **the archive's «Gaspare Cossi» of 1826 was assembled out of an index and a machine transcript, with the act itself saying neither.**

**Still to try**: 1830–1835, and the parish burial register, where a priest would be entered with his title. **He is not at risk** — his sister Celia's act of 1843 names the same parents — **it is his own document that is lost.**

## 21 September — THE ROW'S REMAINING ACTION WAS ALREADY DONE, AND NOBODY NOTICED

This row said «**Still to try: 1830–1835**». **Every one of those years was already read**, and the row that says so is on *What has been read*: «*ANTENATI «Morti, indice» — **thirteen annual volumes**, 55 images, every page's surname column cropped and tiled*», covering **1831–1843**, beside the earlier sweep of **1824–1830**. **The Arienzo death indexes are read continuously from 1824 to 1843.**

**So the negative is much wider than this row believed, and it is bounded by two holes rather than by a year.** Don Giuseppe Cioffi — a **C** — is in none of the twenty years, and the C leaf was opened in each. The two holes are:

- **1834**, whose index is a **single leaf covering A to C and marked END**. C is inside that range, so 1834 is covered for this man, not a hole.
- **1836**, which **does not exist in the index series at all**.

**That leaves exactly one unexamined year before 1844: 1836.** Its death register is `an_ua14338`, 51 images, read for FALCO and not for a priest.

**And the row's own criterion is now nearly met.** It said: «*If he is not in any of them, the reading came from a machine index and must be marked as one*». He is in none of 1824–1843 but 1836. **The reading is therefore recorded as PROBABLY MACHINE-DERIVED, pending 1836** — not retired, because his parents are independently confirmed by his sister **Celia Cioffi**'s act of 3 June 1843.

**The finding behind the finding is about this archive, not about the priest.** A work-list row named volumes to read while the page that records what has been read already said they were done. **Nothing compares a row's «still to try» against `searched.json`**, and this is the second time in two days that a stale instruction has survived the work that answered it.

## CLOSED, 21 September 2026 — 1836 IS READ, AND HE IS NOT IN IT

**`an_ua14338`, all 51 images, swept at the band that carries the dead person's name, age and trade.** That is the one year between 1824 and 1843 with **no index in the series**, and it was the only thing left.

**The year buries EIGHT religious and not one of them is he:** **Don Gennaro Esposito**, *sacerdote*, **ninety**; **Don Alessandro Bruno**, *sacerdote*, **twenty-seven**, son of Don Carlantonio Bruno and Donna Teresa Migliore; **Don Francesco de Gentij**, *sacerdote*, **forty-six**, son of Don Mario de Gentij, *possidente*; a **Diglio** *sacerdote*, son of Pasquale Diglio and Angela Migliore; **Don Antonio Cimmino**, ***seminarista***, **twenty-four**; **Suor Fedele Ruggiero**, *monaca*, **sixty-three**; **Donna Carlotta Rauti**, *monaca*, **seventy-three**; and **Donna Raffaela de' Falco**, *monaca*, **sixty-seven** — the gentry nun this archive already holds, her act confirmed here in passing.

**There is no Giuseppe Cioffi, Crisci or Cossi, sacerdote, aged about fifty-six, in any Arienzo death index or register from 1824 to 1843.** By this row's own criterion the reading is now recorded as **MACHINE-DERIVED**. It is **not retired**: his parents are independently confirmed by his sister **Celia Cioffi**'s act of 3 June 1843, so the man is not in doubt — **only his own document is lost**, and it was never where the citation said.

**The sweep paid for itself twice over**: act 50 of the same volume is **PASQUALE DI GUIDA**, a brother of generation four's mother-in-law.

rows.what: Read act 9 of the 1829 death register — a probable second child for Gioacchino Cioffi and Francesca Falco
rows.note:
**Found in the 1829 *tavola alfabetica* while looking for something else.** «*9. **C[?]ffi LUCA** … [figlio di] **GIOACCHINO** e **FALCO FRANCESCA** … 16 [Gennaio 1829]*».

**The parents are the find.** «GIOACCHINO» with «FALCO FRANCESCA» is a distinctive pair and this archive holds exactly one couple of that description — **GIOACCHINO CIOFFI × FRANCESCA FALCO**, known until now from **a single document**, the 1843 death act of their son ANIELLO, seventy-six. **This would be a second child, and the household's second document in a century of looking.**

**What the index cannot give.** The dead man's surname is in the Crisci/Cossi/Cioffi trap, and an index is written faster than an act. **It gives no age**, so whether Luca is an infant or a grown son of a woman bearing children in the 1760s is unknown — and that decides whether he is a brother of Aniello or something else entirely.

**Act 9 of Arienzo Morti 1829 settles both in one line.** The volume is `an_ua14331`.

## DONE, 20 September 2026 — and it was three findings, not one

**Act 9 is on image 7 RIGHT**, found by sweeping the act numbers across images 4–12. «*è morto nella sua propria casa **LUCA CRISCI, di anni SESSANTA, marito di ANTONIA MORGILLO**, nato in Arienzo, di professione contadino … figlio di **GIOACCHINO CRISCI Defunto** … e di **FRANCESCA FALCO Defunta***», **16 January 1829**, at twenty-four hours.

**1. He is ANIELLO's brother.** Sixty in 1829 gives about **1769**; Aniello, seventy-six in July 1843, about **1767**. **Two years apart, the same two parents.** The household goes from one child to two and from one document to two.

**2. THE SURNAME IS CRISCI, NOT CIOFFI** — and so is the household's. Both acts were magnified, including the 1843 one **this archive had never magnified**, having taken the name from a transcription. **A narrow r, no round o, no double-f ascender.**

**3. Both parents are «Defunto» and «Defunta» in January 1829**, so **Francesca Falco died before then, not merely before 1843** — a window closed by fourteen years. **And Luca had a wife, ANTONIA MORGILLO.**

**The index produced the candidate and the act produced the record**, which is the order this archive insists on. The index could not spell his surname; the act could.

rows.what: Finish the Arienzo civil marriage register for 1815 — images 17 to 30 were never read
rows.note:
**The only register sweep on this archive's shelf with no row against it**, found by reconciling the research log — work-list row 74.

**`an_ua14219`, thirty images, and the volume holds EXACTLY TWENTY-FIVE acts** — fixed by the sindaco's own closing certificate of 31 December 1815, which names act 25 as «*l'ultimo celebrato sul presente Registro*», and corroborated by the divider card in the processetti volume: «*Anno 1815 / Arienzo (66) / dal n° 1 al n° 25*».

**Images 2–16 were read at survey resolution, roughly acts 1 to 13. Images 17 to 30 were never opened** — about twelve marriages, half the year.

**The read half already produced a household**: **SEBASTIANO FALCO × COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO** of San Felice a Cancello, *sapunari* — soap-makers — whose son **LUIGI, eighteen**, married at Arienzo as a minor with both parents consenting in person. **That is one of the five strands on the places figure.** What the unread half holds is unknown, and **a marriage register is the densest thing in this archive**: both spouses, both sets of parents, ages, trades and streets, on one leaf.

**Survey resolution is not a reading.** Even acts 1–13 should be re-read at full magnification before anything in them is quoted — the bride of the Falco act is still «*[?]ietta RENCHIELLO(?)*» and her mother «*[An]gela [?]*».

---

## DONE, 20 September 2026 — and there is no Falco in the unread half

**All ten acts read at 3,200 pixels.** Not twelve: **image *N* right holds act *N−1***, so images 17–30 are acts **16 to 25**, images **24 and 25 are duplicate photographs** of openings already filmed as 22 and 23, image 29 is the closing certificate and image 30 the endboard. The header of this row said «roughly acts 1 to 13» for images 2–16; they are **acts 1 to 15**.

**Loffredo, Morgillo, Verdicchio, Grossi, Carfora, Morgillo, Ferriello, Arrigale, Marletta, Buono** — and no Falco. The year's only Falco remains the soap-maker's son of San Felice a Cancello at act 8, published and still not claimed. The roster of all ten, with both sets of parents, ages, trades and streets, is in `notes/1815-marriage-register-progress.md`.

**Two things the unread half gave.** Act 20 is a **gentry Carfora marriage** — *Signor PASQUALE CARFORA, medico cerusico* of Santa Maria a Vico × *Signora Alessandra de Angelis, gentildonna, of Naples* — naming **PAOLO CARFORA** and **ANNA SABATELLI** dead on **6 November 1782** and **22 January 1789**. **That is material for row 63**, which exists because this archive did not know there were Carfora at Arienzo. And act 21 gives **ELISABETTA COSSI**, daughter of the late **MARINO COSSI** — the **documented Cossi household** this archive has needed while correcting *Cossi* to *Cioffi* on strada Camellara: written twice in one hand as **C + round o + double long ſ + i**, with no *i* after the C and no narrow *r*.

**One age flagged and deliberately not changed.** Act 18 makes **Anna Martone** twenty-nine with a father of forty, and calls her **minore**. The likeliest reading is *diciannove*, but the word was not magnified, so **it stands as written**.

**What remains, and it is now the only thing**: acts 1–15 were read at survey resolution, which this archive does not count as a reading. The bride of the Falco act is still «*[?]ietta RENCHIELLO(?)*» and her mother «*[An]gela [?]*». **Raised as its own row rather than left inside a finished one.**

rows.what: Re-read acts 1–15 of the Arienzo 1815 marriage register at full resolution
rows.note:
**Images 2–16 of `an_ua14219` were read at SURVEY resolution only**, and this archive's standing rule is that survey resolution is not a reading. Row 81 finished acts 16–25 at 3,200 pixels and found ten acts' worth of names the survey had not given; the same is owed to acts 1–15.

**The specific debt is inside the one act that matters.** Act 8 is the Falco of San Felice a Cancello — **LUIGI FALCO**, eighteen, *sapunaro*, son of **SEBASTIANO FALCO** and **COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO** — and **the bride is still unread**: «*[?]ietta RENCHIELLO(?)*», of strada del Borgo, with her mother «*[An]gela [?]*», fifty-six. A household published with an unreadable spouse is a household that cannot be searched for anywhere else.

**Cheap**: fifteen acts, one render each, using the layout row 81 established — image *N* right holds act *N−1*, each act starting on a right page and running onto the next left page.

---

## ACT 8 IS DONE, AND IT WAS WORTH DOING FIRST

**The bride is read.** «*è comparsa egualmente **STELLA PETRILLO** di anni **diciotto**, domiciliata in questa suddetta comune, **strada del Borgo**, di professione **filatrice**, **MINORE**, assistita da **BRIGIDA COSSI** sua madre di anni **cinquantasei**, di professione contadina, domiciliata colla figlia, essendo morto il padre **SABBATINO PETRILLO***» — and the groom is «**LUIGI FALCO** di anni **diciotto compiti**, di professione **SAPUNARO**, domiciliato nel comune de' **SEI CASALI**, strada **Croce di San Felice**, **MINORE**», with **SEBASTIANO FALCO** of the same trade and **COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO**, fifty-five, *filatrice*. **19 Mar 1815**, before Daniele Loria, sindaco.

**Three corrections came out of one act.** Her forename: the act says **STELLA**, the index says **GIULIA**, and this archive had **«Giustina»**, which is neither — the parents are identical in both documents so the woman is not in doubt, only her name. Her mother: **BRIGIDA**, not the «[An]gela [?]» the note carried. And her surname went the other way: **at survey width the act reads «Vecchiello»**, which is what this pass was about to publish, and **at twelve times it is PETRILLO**. *A word that changes when you magnify it was never read.*

**And the surname test this archive relies on was narrowed.** «COSSI» here descends exactly as a double f would, so the descender does not separate it from «Cioffi» in this hand. **The letter count does**: *Cioffi* carries an i between the C and the o and *Cossi* does not. Three instances in this one volume say so. On /corrections as a method entry.

**Fourteen acts remain** — 1 to 7 and 9 to 15.

---

## DONE — ALL FIFTEEN ACTS READ AT 3,200 PIXELS, 21 September 2026

**The volume is now read end to end**, both halves, every act at full resolution. The roster with both sets of parents, ages, trades and streets is in `notes/1815-marriage-register-progress.md`.

**IMAGE 14 IS A DUPLICATE PHOTOGRAPH OF IMAGE 13** — the same act 13 filmed twice. That is the extra leaf that made image *N* right hold act *N* up to image 13 and act *N−1* from image 15 on. With images 24 and 25 duplicating 22 and 23, **the volume contains three duplicate photographs**.

**AND THE FALCO ACT IS 19 MARCH, NOT 19 MAY.** The date had stood as «19 [May] 1815», bracketed; **hours earlier today the bracket was removed and «19 May» published as fact**, in the entry that read the bride's name off the act for the first time. The word is **MARZO**, and **the register's own order proves it without reading the word at all**: act 7 is 16 March, act 9 is 21 March, act 10 is 6 April, and the volume runs in **strict date order** from 4 February to 2 December. A 19 May at act 8 is impossible. On /corrections.

**Five COSSI in one volume in one hand** — Brigida, Chiara, Faustina, Elisabetta and Marino — every one written *C + round o + double long ſ + i* with **no i between the C and the o**. The surname is settled and the strada Camellara correction was about one household.

**Three things for other rows.** **DOROTEA CARFORA**, 49, a *bracciale*'s wife of strada Rosciano, born about 1766 — a third social register of Carfora for row 63, joined to neither the gentry surgeon of act 20 nor the *contadini* of 1831. **MARGARITA DI GUIDA**, dead at Arienzo **15 October 1814**, named in act 1 — a lead for rows 39 and 40, claimed as nothing. And **two strada Camellara households**, the Melillo and the Verdicchio shoemakers.

**One caution recorded rather than resolved**: at contact-sheet resolution the 1815 marriage **index** appeared to number Michele Monaco **13** where the register numbers him **15**. The index was not read at magnification, so **nothing is claimed**.

rows.what: Check every work-list «still to try» against what the coverage page says has been read
rows.note:
**Row 79 told this archive to read six volumes that `searched.json` already recorded as read** — the Arienzo death indexes for 1830–1835, part of a continuous sweep of **1824 to 1843**. The row would have sent a reader to open all six for nothing, and it had been standing since the row was raised.

**Neither file knows the other exists.** A work-list row's «still to try» is a claim about what has NOT been done; `searched.json` is the register of what HAS been. **Nothing compares them**, in either direction — so a row can ask for finished work, and a finished search can go unrecorded in the row that wanted it.

**What to build.** A gate is probably not writable: the two files name sources in prose, not by key, and a regular expression over «1830–1835» against «1831–1843» is a range-parsing problem with a long tail. **What IS writable is a report** — pull every «still to try», «next» and «remains» sentence out of the open rows, pull every `src` and `when` out of `searched.json`, and print them side by side by ark and by year for a human to read in one pass. **One reading, not a build step.**

**Why it is worth a row of its own.** This is the third instance in three days of the archive's own files disagreeing while both are right about their own contents: the two households files disagreeing about evidence text, the corrections page standing after the findings that overturned it, and now the work list against the coverage page. **At this size the archive's largest source of wasted work is no longer the sources — it is not knowing what it already holds.**

---

## BUILT AND RUN — `tools/staleness_report.py`

**Sixteen hits across twenty-three open rows, and every one of them is row 79.** Nothing false anywhere else. The report pulls every «still to try / what remains / never opened / next» sentence out of the open rows, takes the years and the SERIES out of each, and prints it beside any coverage row covering the same years in the same series.

**It is a report and not a gate, on purpose.** `searched.json` has a structured `when` and names the ark; a work-list row names years **in prose, inside an argument**, and often names no ark at all — row 79's six volumes exist only as the string «1830–1835». Matching those is a judgement about whether two prose descriptions mean the same shelf, and **a row may be re-reading a volume at higher resolution on purpose** (row 82 is doing exactly that to `an_ua14219`). A gate here would either cry wolf or miss the case it was written for.

**Matching on the year alone does not work, and two things had to be added before the output was readable.**

1. **The SERIES has to match as well as the year.** Arienzo has deaths, births, marriages and an index series for each, in the same years. «1830–1835 read» answers «1830–1835 still to try» only if both mean the same shelf — so an index is kept apart from the register it indexes.
2. **«ANTENATI» contains «nati».** Every row in both files names Antenati, so on the first run every row was classified as a BIRTH row and the report was all noise. Six of the twenty-two hits died with that one substitution.

**And a third, which is about honesty rather than noise.** A coverage row spanning a century — a commercial index, a whole parish harvest — **overlaps every question ever asked and answers none of them**. Those are marked **WIDE** and hidden by default rather than dropped, because «FindMyPast covers 1806–1900» is true and useless, and a report that silently discarded it would be hiding a row rather than ranking it. `--all` shows them.

**Ark matching, which was the obvious approach, is nearly worthless here**: only **four** arks are named both in an open row and on the coverage page, and all four are explainable. The miss that cost six volumes named **no ark at all**.

**The Capodiuomo rows are concentrated and they have a shape.** Ten years of death-register progress notes carry them — **1817 (11), 1818 (9), 1819 (5), 1820 (8), 1821 (10), 1822 (14), 1823 (25), 1824 (9), 1825 (1)** — and then almost nothing until a single instance each in 1837 and 1838. **That is the fingerprint of a reading habit in one stretch of work, not of a street that existed for eight years and stopped.**

**What is actually established.** Two acts were read at **3,000 pixels** on 20 September 2026 — `an_ua14324` img34r act 65 and `an_ua14325` img55r act 51 — and both read **CAPODICONCA**, the word appearing three times in the first. **Nothing else has been magnified.** The correction published that day over-generalised from those two and has been amended.

**And the negative evidence points one way.** The Arienzo BIRTH registers for **1832 and 1836**, read out act by act on 21 September, give **strada Capodiconca** constantly and **strada Capodiuomo not once**.

**How to settle it cheaply.** Take five Capodiuomo rows from different years — 1817, 1819, 1821, 1823, 1837 — render each act at 3,000 px and magnify the word. **If all five read Capodiconca the street is one and 228 rows need correcting**; if any reads Capodiuomo, Arienzo had two streets and both corrections stand as written. **Five images decide a word that appears nine hundred times.**

---

## SETTLED THE SAME DAY — SIX ACTS, AND IT IS CAPODICONCA

**Five images were budgeted; six were read, chosen to span both ends and the middle of the run.** **1817 act 11, 1819 act 23, 1821 act 15, 1822 act 65, 1823 act 51, 1824 act 5** — every one **CAPODICONCA**, several twice in one act, and the 1824 act in a hand so clear it needs no magnification at all.

**219 rows corrected** in `data/sweep-people.tsv`, the published register and nine years of notes. **Eleven left alone**: the 1837 and 1838 rows, because **that hand is too rapid to decide at this scan's limit**. A word this archive cannot read is not a word it may change.

**The distribution was the tell and it is worth keeping.** 1817–1825 held 219 of the 228, then nothing for eleven years, then nine stragglers. **A name that appears heavily for one continuous stretch of work and then stops is a reading habit, not a fact about the town.** Checking the *distribution* of a doubtful reading across the corpus cost one command and pointed at the answer before any image was opened.

rows.what: Re-sweep six birth registers at the DECLARANT band — the parents band alone can miss a Falco father
rows.note:
**The gap, stated plainly.** In the Arienzo birth registers an act opens on a RIGHT page and the parents are named at the top of the NEXT LEFT page — **but only when somebody other than the father presents the child**. When the **father** declares, the left page says «*da lui dichiarante*» and **his name appears only on the right page**. A sweep of the parents band therefore reads every **mother** and misses a **father** whose wife is not herself a Falco.

**How it was found.** Two 1836 death acts give **SALVATORE FALCO** at fourteen months and **PASQUALINA FALCO** at sixteen — births in mid-1835 — and 1835 had just been published here as holding no Falco. Salvatore's mother is a **VIGLIOTTA**: if his father declared, the parents band could never have seen him.

**Already closed**: **1834, 1835 and 1836** have now been read at **both** bands. All three still hold no Falco, so the two children remain unaccounted for — but the nils are now sound.

**Still owed a second band: 1820–1823, 1829, 1831, 1832, 1833, 1837, 1838.** 1820 is exempt — each act fits on one page there, so the single band caught both parents. **Roughly sixty contact sheets at `--band 0.34 0.19 --half R --cols 4 --width 1600`.**

**Why it is worth the second pass.** Every nil this row touches was published as a negative, and **a negative is the most expensive thing this archive can get wrong** — nobody re-checks one. Two of them are already known to be incomplete in principle; the rest are untested.

## VINDICATED ON THE FIRST VOLUME IT TOUCHED — 21 September 2026

**1821, declarant band, act 22: ROSARIA FALCO, born 15 March 1821** to **GIUSEPPE FALCO, thirty-eight**, and **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA, thirty-seven**, of strada Camellara. **The mother is a Vigliotta, so the parents band could never have seen her** — and that band is what this archive had published 1821 on.

**It also broke a discriminator.** This household is the one the archive places on **strada COSTA**; here it is on **strada CAMELLARA**. On /corrections.

## 1822 AND 1823 READ OUT — 21 September 2026

**Both years hold exactly one Falco declarant each, and the archive already had both.** 1822 act 8 is **GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO**, presenting Angela Maria; 1823 act 38 is **GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty-two, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara**, presenting Pasqua. **278 images read; nothing new.**

## 1829 READ OUT, AND 1831 SHOULD NEVER HAVE BEEN ON THIS LIST — 21 September 2026

**1829: no Falco declarant at all.** The year is carried by midwives — **ROSA DELLA SELVA, seventy-eight**, and **CATERINA RUGGIERO, seventy-one** — so in a year like this the parents band is the stronger instrument and the declarant band returns the same two names over and over. **Its *tavola* is a blank printed form**: 1829 has no index and never had one, which makes the act-by-act pass the only instrument there is.

**1831 was already done at both bands and this row said otherwise.** The coverage page's own first sentence reads «*RE-READ at the PARENTS band; the earlier pass swept the DECLARANT line*». A hundred images were read a third time on this row's instruction. **`tools/staleness_report.py` exists to catch exactly that and printed nothing**, because «*still owed*» was not a trigger phrase and «*remaining*» is not «*remains*». The tool has been widened; the episode is on /corrections.

## AND THEN IT FOUND A CHILD OF THE DIRECT LINE — 1832, act 84

**MARIA CARMELA FALCO, born 10 October 1832**, in her father's own house on strada Camellara, to **VINCENZO FALCO, forty**, and **ANDREANA CRISCI, thirty-six**. **This archive had published that this couple had no child in 1832**, after reading the whole volume at the parents band.

**The act states the failure outright.** The left page reads «*nata da ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legittima … **E DA LUI DICHIARANTE**, di anni come sopra, di professione come sopra, domiciliato come sopra*». **The father's name is nowhere on the page this archive reads for parents.** No index rescues it either: the 1832 *tavola* stops at **C**.

**Row 85 has now paid twice in one day** — Rosaria Falco in 1821, Maria Carmela Falco in 1832 — and the second one is generation three. **Every year still on this list was published as a negative on the band that cannot see this.**

**1833: no Falco declarant**, in a year carried by the two midwives again. One candidate opened and excluded — **VINCENZO CALCAGNO**, forty, contadino, at image 109, which is what Vincenzo Falco's age and trade would have been.

## THE LIST IS FINISHED — AND 1838 WAS THE WORST OF THEM

**1837**: one Falco declarant, **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO** at act 108, which is the Raffaele Falco this archive already held. Nothing new.

**1838 — the year this archive had published as «NO FALCO AT ALL» — holds TWO Falco births.** Act 79, **9 September: STANISLAO FALCO**, to **VINCENZO FALCO, forty-six**, and **ANDREANA CRISCI, forty**, of strada Camellara — **a son of generation three whose birth act had never been found**; the archive knew him only from his wedding of 1861. And act 77, **4 September: MARINO ALESSANDRO FALCO**, to **MICHELANGELO FALCO, thirty-four**, and **MARIA MIGLIORE, thirty-five**, of strada Sant'Andrea — **a third wife for Michelangelo Falco in seven years**, on a street neither of the others is on.

**Both left pages say «*e da lui dichiarante*» and never write the father's name.** The old row even reported «no Crisci» in a year where Andreana Crisci is named in full on one of them.

## WHAT THE ROW PRODUCED, IN ONE DAY

**Nine volumes re-read; four Falco births recovered** — ROSARIA (1821), MARIA CARMELA (1832), STANISLAO and MARINO ALESSANDRO (both 1838) — **three of them into households this archive already had, two of them into the direct line.** Three published statements corrected besides: a coverage row that had left **Pasqua Falco's birth act out of its own year**, her **street**, and an 1821 contact-sheet candidate that was a **COSCI**. And one process fix: `tools/staleness_report.py` could not see this row's own «still owed» and now can.

**Done: 1821, 1822, 1823, 1829, 1832, 1833, 1837, 1838 — and 1831, which never needed it. Exempt: 1820. NOTHING REMAINS ON THIS ROW.**

## WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND

**The two bands are not alternatives and this archive should stop treating a single-band sweep as a reading.** Every Arienzo birth register read at one band only is a nil of unknown strength. The nine years on this row were the ones already suspected; **the rest of the series has never been tested.**

rows.note:

**The rule, in the act's own words.** When the father presents his own child the left page says «*è nato da [MOTHER] sua moglie legittima … **E DA LUI DICHIARANTE**, di anni come sopra, di professione come sopra, domiciliato come sopra*» — **and never writes his name**. A parents-band sweep sees the mother's surname and nothing else. **So a Falco father whose wife is not a Falco is invisible at any resolution.**

**TWO GROUPS OF YEARS.**

**(a) Read at the parents band only** — the nil is of unknown strength: **1816** (`an_ua14413`), **1817** (`an_ua14414`), **1818** (`an_ua14415`), **1834** (`an_ua14431` — already done at both), **1835** (`an_ua14432` — done), **1836** (`an_ua14433` — done). *So the real remainder here is 1816, 1817 and 1818*, and **1817's outcome is «no Falco»**, the same kind of statement that failed in 1838.

**(b) No coverage row exists at all**: **1819**, **1824**, **1825**, **1826**, **1827**, **1828**, **1830**. Single acts from 1824, 1825, 1826 and 1828 are cited in households, which means those volumes were *opened at one page*. **Nobody can say whether they were read**, and that is precisely the state /searched exists to prevent. 1826 and 1827 are row 35's and are being read now.

**Cost.** About 1,300 images across ten volumes, which is **roughly fifty-five contact sheets** at `--band 0.34 0.19 --half R --cols 4 --width 1600`, plus the parents band for the years that have never had one. **Row 85 took one day for nine volumes.**

**Why it is worth it, stated plainly.** Generation three bore children across this whole span — Luigi 1819, Giuseppe Nunzio 1824, Angelandrea 1826, Sara 1828, Pasquale 1830, Maria Carmela 1832, Pasquale the second 1834, Stanislao 1838, Antonio 1843 — **and two of those, Maria Carmela and Stanislao, were found only yesterday, in volumes this archive had called read.** A gap year in that series is a missing child until a reading at both bands says otherwise.

## THE THIRD INSTRUMENT, AND WHAT IT MAKES REDUNDANT — 21 September 2026

**Reading 1826 and 1827 produced a rule that halves this row.** There are three ways into one of these volumes and they do not overlap the way they look as though they do:

- **The TAVOLA** indexes the **child's surname**, with both parents named. **So a complete tavola answers the question «did a FALCO FATHER register a child this year?» outright** — the child is a Falco and is filed under F.
- **The PARENTS band** is the only instrument that finds a **FALCO MOTHER**, because her child is filed in the tavola under her husband's surname. That is how **MARIA FALCO's son of 1826** and **ROSA FALCO's daughter of 1827** were missed for years.
- **The DECLARANT band** finds a Falco father whose left page says «*e da lui dichiarante*». **It is redundant wherever the tavola is complete**, and it is the expensive one.

**So the cheap route is TAVOLA + PARENTS BAND, and the declarant band only where the tavola fails.** And it fails often enough to matter: **1829's tavola is a blank printed form**, **1832's stops at C**, **1823's is under a paper slip**, and **1838's leaf was never filmed past the recto**. **1826's and 1827's are complete through the whole alphabet** and both were checked against the page-break rule.

**Check the tavola first. It is one opening and it decides how much of the volume has to be read.**

## FOUR VOLUMES OFF THE LIST — 21 September 2026

**1824, 1825, 1826 and 1827 are read end to end at both bands** and are on /searched. Two new children came out of them — **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI (1826)** and **MARIA CARMELA MORGILLO (1827)**, both through **Falco mothers**, which is the half of the problem the tavole cannot answer — together with a second Andreana Crisci, two corrected act numbers and a death act that had been harvested without being held.

**REMAINING: 1819, 1828 and 1830, which have no coverage row at all; and 1816, 1817 and 1818, read at the parents band only. 1817's outcome is «no Falco» — the same kind of statement that failed in 1838.**

## 1828 DONE, AND THE TAVOLA RULE PAID FOR ITSELF

**MARIANTONIA CIOFFI, born 8 March 1828** to Francesco Cioffi and **MARIA FALCO** — **her death act, already held, says seven months old on 23 October, and she was seven months and fifteen days.** A life closed from both ends.

**REMAINING: 1819 (different format — prose, two acts an opening, one band catches both parents) and 1830; then 1816, 1817 and 1818, read at the parents band only.**

## 1819 READ OUT — TWO NEW CHILDREN, BOTH THROUGH FALCO MOTHERS

**ALESSANDRA DIGLIO, 27 April 1819** (act 52), to Alfonso Diglio and **MARIA FALCO** — and **her father signed his own name** where both witnesses could not write. **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI, 7 June 1819** (act 68), to Francesco Cioffi and **MARIA FALCO** — **a child this archive held only as a death**, 25 March 1824 aged five; born 7 June 1819 he was five years and nine months.
