**The 1819 volume is in the older Napoleonic format** — running prose, two acts to an opening — so **one band catches declarant and mother together**: `--band 0.17 0.28 --half LR --cols 4 --width 2400`, six tiles to a sheet. Its *tavola* survives only as its last page, numbered XI, with the child's-name column lost in the gutter.

**REMAINING: 1830, which has no coverage row at all; and 1816, 1817 and 1818, read at the parents band only.**

## 1830 READ OUT — AND IT IS THE CASE FOR RUNNING BOTH BANDS, IN ONE VOLUME

**Two Falco children born on 24 March 1830, to two households on strada Camellara, and this archive had neither act.** **PASQUALE FALCO** (act 42, six in the morning) to Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci — the civil act for a child known only from a machine-read baptism and a death. **ANNA FALCO** (act 43, eleven) to Michelangelo Falco and Antonia Vigliotta — **new**, and her death act's «*di mesi TREDICI*» closes to ten days.

**EACH BAND FOUND ONE AND NEITHER WOULD HAVE FOUND BOTH.** Act 42 says «*e da lui dichiarante*» and names no Falco on the parents page. Act 43 was presented by a midwife and names no Falco on the declarant page. **And the 1830 tavola is under the archivist's card**, so there was no third route.

**REMAINING ON THIS ROW: 1816, 1817 and 1818, read at the PARENTS band only.** 1817's outcome is «no Falco» — the same kind of statement that failed in 1838.

## 1816 READ OUT — NO NEW FALCO, AND THE BEST FIND OF THE ROW

**SARA RUGGIERO — generation three's mother-in-law — WAS A MIDWIFE.** Act 29 of 1816: «*è comparsa **SARA RUGGIERO, di anni QUARANTACINQUE, di professione LEVATRICE, domiciliata in detto Comune, strada CAMELLARA***». This archive holds a Sara Ruggiero, forty-five, of strada Camellara, in the 1817 register as **Arcangelo Crisci's wife**.

**And it explains the ten pages.** «*Matrina fuit SARA RUGGIERO*» stands on ten pages of the parish baptism harvest, godmother across **six Falco households**, and the archive had no account of it. **A levatrice stands godmother to the children she delivers.** *Three Ruggiero women delivered this town — Sara, Caterina and Gelsomina — across twenty years.*

**The 1816 tavola is under the archivist's card as well**, which makes **six** volumes: 1816, 1823, 1824, 1825, 1830, 1846. Work-list row 10 is now about a policy, not a leaf.

**REMAINING ON THIS ROW: 1817 and 1818.** Both are in the same prose format as 1816 and 1819, so **one band does declarant and mother together** — `--band 0.17 0.28 --half LR --cols 4 --width 2400`, and the sweeps are already rendered. **1817's outcome is «no Falco», the same kind of statement that failed in 1838.**

## 1817 READ OUT — THE SECOND «NO FALCO» OVERTURNED IN ONE DAY

**SALVATORE DIGLIO, 15 May 1817** (act 49), to Alfonso Diglio and **MARIA FALCO** of strada Camellara — **new**, and the first of two Salvatore in that house. **And GIOVANNA MORGILLO, 22 September 1817** (act 69), to Carlantonio Morgillo and **ROSA FALCO**, a daughter of the founders — **which this archive has cited from this very volume, image 36 left, since before this week.** The coverage page and the household file were contradicting each other about the year.

**Three di Guida acts came with it**, and one closes a prediction: **MADDALENA DI GUIDA, 25 May 1817**, to **ANGELANDREA DI GUIDA DI GIUSEPPE** — the archive had predicted she was «*named for her grandmother Maddalena Rivetta*» and here is the birth, with «di Giuseppe» corroborating the parish filiation from a civil document five months before her father's death. **PASQUALE DI GUIDA** is **forty-two and a MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA** in June 1817, which dates his unread baptism year to about 1775.

**REMAINING ON THIS ROW: 1818 alone** — 85 images, same prose format, sweep already rendered.

## 1818 READ OUT — THE ROW IS FINISHED

**MARIA CARMELA, 18 January 1818**, to **DOMENICO COSSI** of strada Cossi and **MARGARITA FALCO, forty** — **new**, and the earliest act that household has. Raffaele Falco (act 47) and Maddalena Falco (June) confirmed.

**The volume holds the year twice** — a printed slip declares the 1817 register stock «*vale pel corrente Esercizio 1818*» — so act 9 could be read in two hands. **Both say COSSI**, where this archive's household is called COSPI and an 1819 index makes the son a CRISCI. **Three spellings, three documents, one household**; published as a question, and the household is not renamed.

## WHAT THE WHOLE ROW PRODUCED

**Ten volumes read end to end — 1816, 1817, 1818, 1819, 1824, 1825, 1826, 1827, 1828, 1830 — and nine children recovered**: Giuseppe Cioffi (1819), Alessandra Diglio (1819), Salvatore Diglio (1817), Maria Carmela of Margarita Falco (1818), Giuseppe Cioffi the second (1826), Maria Carmela Morgillo (1827), Mariantonia Cioffi (1828), Pasquale Falco and Anna Falco (both 24 March 1830). **Every one of them came through a FALCO MOTHER or a «*da lui dichiarante*», and no index could have reached any of them.**

**TWO PUBLISHED NILS OVERTURNED** — 1817 and 1838, both «no Falco», the strongest negative this archive publishes. **Three di Guida acts** recovered, one of them closing a prediction the archive had made from a name. **SARA RUGGIERO found to be a midwife**, which explains ten parish pages the archive could not account for. **Two act numbers corrected** by the register's own order. And **six volumes found to carry the same archivist's card across their index** — 1816, 1823, 1824, 1825, 1830, 1846 — which turns work-list row 10 from a leaf into a policy.

**NOTHING REMAINS ON THIS ROW.**

rows.what: FRANCESCO FALCO and FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO — two men, or one filiation wrong
rows.note:
**Raised 21 September 2026, from act 20 of the Arienzo marriage register for 1854** — a volume nobody here had opened.

**The act says:** «***FRANCESCO FALCO maggiore**, di anni **quarantotto**, nato in Arienzo, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **strada CAMELLARA**, figlio del **fu RAFFAELE** … e della **fu CHIARA RIVETTI** … **VEDOVO DI RAFFAELA FALCO***».

**This archive says:** **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO**, married **16 July 1832**, entered as a child of **PASQUALE FALCO and Chiara Rivetti** — and his wife is a **RAFFAELA FALCO**, the two of them being the parents of **PASQUALINA FALCO**, dead 1836.

**One wife's name, two fathers.** Either there are two men, or one of the filiations is wrong.

**IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE MICHELE-AND-MICHELANGELO PROBLEM, WHICH WAS SETTLED ON 20 SEPTEMBER AND WENT THE OTHER WAY.** There, two names that looked like one man were two — **MICHELANGELO a son of Pasquale, MICHELE a son of Raffaele** — and both married an **Antonia Vigliotti**. Here the pattern repeats to the letter: two forms of one forename, two fathers of those same two names, and **wives who share a name**. *Which is a reason to expect two men and not a reason to conclude it.*

**How to settle it, cheapest first.**
1. **Read the 1832 marriage act.** This archive has Francescantonio's marriage from an **index**, and an index is not an act. Arienzo Matrimoni 1832 = `an_ua14236`. **The act will name his father.**
2. **Pasqualina Falco's death act of 1836** — `an_ua14338` — already read here for Margarita Falco. It names her parents; whether it says Francesco or Francescantonio is the second discriminator.
3. **Raffaela Falco's own death act.** Francesco is her widower by August 1854 and the Arienzo death registers **1844–1858 are read out** — so if she died in that window she has already been seen, and if she has not, she died before 1844.

**Nothing is to be merged until one of the three is read.** Both readings stand in the household file, each beside the other.

---

## TEST 1 RUN — 22 September 2026. THE INDEX WAS RIGHT, AND THAT MAKES IT WORSE

**Arienzo, Matrimoni 1832, act 8** (`an_ua14236` img 9R), read from the act:

> «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO, maggiore**, di anni **ventisei**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi strada CAMELLARA**, figlio di **PASQUALE FALCO** —, di professione contadino, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **CHIARA RIVETTI**, di professione contadina, domiciliata **ivi**; e **RAFFAELA FALCO, MINORE**, di anni **diciannove** … figlia di **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di professione **COLONO**, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANTONINA DI GUIDA**, domiciliata ivi*»

**PASQUALE. The clerk drew a dash where «defunto» goes and left it empty.**

### The two acts now line up field for field

| | **1832, act 8** | **1854, act 20** |
|---|---|---|
| name | Francescantonio Falco | Francesco Falco |
| age | 26 → **b. c.1806** | 48 → **b. c.1806** |
| trade | contadino | contadino |
| street | **strada Camellara** | **strada Camellara** |
| father | **PASQUALE**, *alive* | **fu RAFFAELE** |
| mother | **CHIARA RIVETTI**, *alive* | **fu CHIARA RIVETTI** |
| wife | **RAFFAELA FALCO** | *widower of* **RAFFAELA FALCO** |

**Everything agrees except the father — and neither act contradicts itself.** Pasquale Falco died **1 October 1834**, twenty-seven months after being called living in 1832. Raffaele Falco was dead before **February 1850**. **Both filiations are internally sound.**

### What that leaves

**Either two men of one name, born the same year, on the same street, each with a mother called CHIARA RIVETTI and a wife called RAFFAELA FALCO** — which is the Michele-and-Michelangelo answer, and it was the right answer there — **or one clerk wrote one wrong forename.**

**AND A THIRD HUSBAND HAS TURNED UP.** This archive also holds «**Michelangelo Falco & Raffaela Falco**», from a death act of **16 March 1834**. **Three men, three households, one wife's name.** *Michelangelo is a son of Pasquale. Francescantonio is a son of Pasquale. Francesco is a son of Raffaele.* **The overlap is no longer a coincidence to explain away; it is the shape of the problem.**

### The next test, and it is cheaper than any of the three first listed

**RAFFAELA FALCO WAS NINETEEN AND A MINOR IN JULY 1832, SO BORN ABOUT 1813, AND SHE IS A DAUGHTER OF GIUSEPPE FALCO AND ANTONIA DI GUIDA.** Her birth act should be in the Arienzo births of **1812–1814** — `an_ua14409`–`an_ua14411` — **three volumes this archive has never opened**, and they are on the 1809–1815 list row 9 has just been corrected to name.

**If there is ONE Raffaela Falco of that generation, the three households are one and two of the three husbands are spellings.** *If there are two, the Michele answer applies again.* **Nothing is merged until that act is read.**

### 1813 read out the same day — she is not in it

`an_ua14410`, **53 acts, every one read**. **One Falco in the year**, and it is the *other* Giuseppe Falco: act 2 of **5 January 1813**, «*GIUSEPPE FALCO, trentatré, contadino, **strada COSTA** … da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA** … un maschio … **ANTONIO***». **No Raffaela Falco. No Antonia di Guida.**

**Nineteen in July 1832 means born between July 1812 and July 1813**, so the window is now **1812 alone** — `an_ua14409`, 93 images — **and its second half first.** *1814 (`an_ua14411`) is outside the window unless the clerk rounded her age down, which these clerks do.*

### 1812 read out too — and there is no Falco in it at all

`an_ua14409`, **93 images, every act read**. **Not one Falco in the year**, as father, mother or child. With 1813 done the same day, **the whole of her stated birth window is covered and she is absent from it**.

**So one of three things.** Her age was rounded — *the same day's reading produced a groom called «thirty-two» whose birth act makes him thirty-one* — which puts **1811** (`an_ua14408`) and **1814** (`an_ua14411`) next. Or **she was not born at Arienzo**. Or her birth was never registered.

**The 1812 tavola cannot shortcut it**: image 92 is «*Tavola Annuale Alfabetica de' Nati … Anno 1812*», alphabetical by the child's forename, and the archivist's card **«THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY»** covers all but its first page. **1812 joins the blocked-index list.**

### A THIRD CHIARA RIVETTI — 22 September 2026

**MARIA FALCO, wife of Francesco Cioffi of strada Camellara**, died 1 May 1862, and her act (`an_ua14364` img 19R, act 33) calls her «*figlia del **fu GIUSEPPE**, di professione contadino … e della **fu CHIARA RIVETTI***».

**So the tally is now:**

| husband | wife | how this archive got him |
|---|---|---|
| **PASQUALE FALCO** | Chiara Rivetti | a household of long standing |
| **RAFFAELE FALCO** | Chiara Rivetti | separated from Pasquale on 20 Sep 2026, by magnifying one capital **R** |
| **GIUSEPPE FALCO** | Chiara Rivetti | this act, read at 3× on 22 Sep 2026 |

**Three forenames, one wife's name, one street.** And the same pattern already sits at the head of this row for **MICHELE / MICHELANGELO** and **FRANCESCO / FRANCESCANTONIO**, each pair splitting between a father Pasquale and a father Raffaele.

**THAT IS NOW A PATTERN AND NOT THREE COINCIDENCES.** Either the Falco of strada Camellara really did run three brothers who each married a Chiara Rivetti — which is not credible — or **CHIARA RIVETTI is one woman and the clerks of Arienzo wrote her husband's forename three different ways across forty years.** *If that is so, then Michele and Michelangelo are one man, Francesco and Francescantonio are one man, and the correction of 20 September went the wrong way.*

**Nothing is merged on this reasoning.** What would settle it is **Chiara Rivetti's own death act**, which names her husband once and for all — and the Arienzo deaths are read act by act for **1844–1862** with no Chiara Rivetti in them, so **she died before 1844**, in the years this archive has read only in part.

---

## MICHELANGELO'S OWN ACT, AND THE CASE FOR ONE MAN — 22 September 2026

**Arienzo, Matrimoni 1828, act 17, 6 December** (`an_ua14232` img 18R), read from the act:

> «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **MICHELANGELO FALCO, MINORE**, di anni **ventiquattro**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi strada CAMELLARA**, **figlio di PASQUALE FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **CHIARA RI=/VETTI**, domiciliata **ivi**; ed **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, MAGGIORE**, di anni ventisette … figlia di **FRANCESCO VIGLIOTTA DEFUNTO** … e di **VITTORIA REPETELLA***»

### The two acts, field by field

| | **1828, act 17** | **1850, act 6** |
|---|---|---|
| name | **MICHELANGELO** Falco, *minore* | **MICHELE** Falco |
| age | 24 → **b. c.1804** | 43 → **b. c.1807** |
| trade | contadino | colono |
| street | **strada Camellara** | **strada Camellara** |
| father | **PASQUALE**, *alive* | **fu RAFFAELE** |
| mother | **CHIARA RIVETTI**, *alive* | **fu CHIARA RIVETTI** |
| wife | **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** | *widower of* **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, remarrying |

### Three things this archive already held, which nobody had put together

**One. Both parents die between the two acts, in the right order.** **PASQUALE FALCO died 1 October 1834**; **CHIARA RIVETTI died 13 September 1843**. In February 1850 both would be marked dead, and the 1850 act marks both dead. **Its only disagreement with 1828 is the father's forename.**

**Two. There is exactly ONE Chiara Rivetti death in the Arienzo registers, and she is Pasquale's widow.** The civil deaths are now read act by act for **1816 to 1865** — fifty consecutive years. The single act is **13 September 1843**: «*CHIARA RIVETTI **VEDOVA DI PASQUALE FALCO**, nata in Arienzo, di anni **OTTANTA***». **If a second Chiara Rivetti had been married to a Raffaele Falco and died before February 1850, she should be in those fifty years. She is not.**

**Three. The parish says the same.** The Arienzo baptisms hold **«MICHELE ANGELO ANTONIO FALCO, baptised 25 September 1808, mother CHIARA RIVETTI»** — *a machine transcription, unverified, and named as such.* **A child christened «Michele Angelo Antonio» can be called MICHELE by one clerk and MICHELANGELO by another for the rest of his life.**

### What this does to the correction of 20 September

That correction split the two men **on one magnified capital R**, and it was careful and well argued. **The weight has now moved the other way**, and it has moved on records this archive already held. *Either two men of one christening name, born three years apart on one street, each with a mother called Chiara Rivetti and a wife called Antonia Vigliotta — or one man and one clerk's slip.*

**NOTHING IS MERGED.** Both households stand, each pointing at the other. **What would settle it is his own death act**: he was alive on **7 February 1862**, declaring his son Pasquale's death, and the Arienzo deaths are read to 1865 with no Michele or Michelangelo Falco in them — **so he died after 1865, where this archive cannot follow**, which is exactly where Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida went too. *The next best is the 1808 baptism read from the image, which names the father; it is a FamilySearch full-text page and sits behind row 18.*

---

## HALF OF THIS ROW IS SETTLED — 22 September 2026

**FRANCESCO FALCO of 1854 IS FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO of 1832.** The chain is three records this archive already held:

1. **6 Jul 1832**, from the act — **RAFFAELA FALCO**, of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida, marries **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO**, «*figlio di **PASQUALE FALCO** … e di **CHIARA RIVETTI***», strada Camellara.
2. **20 Apr 1854**, cited on the register page — «***RAFFAELA FALCO, 34, contadina, strada CAMELLARA, MOGLIE DI FRANCESCO FALCO***», parents **Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida**.
3. **Aug 1854**, four months later — a **FRANCESCO FALCO** of strada Camellara marries again as «***VEDOVO DI RAFFAELA FALCO***».

**So the 1854 act's «figlio del fu RAFFAELE» is a clerk's error**, and the household «Raffaele Falco & Chiara Rivetti», created here on 21 September, rests on it. *It is left standing with the correction attached.* **See the corrections page.**

### What is left

**Only the MICHELE / MICHELANGELO half**, and it now leans the same way: Michelangelo's own act says **PASQUALE**; the parish christened a son of that couple **MICHELE ANGELO ANTONIO** in 1808; both men are of strada Camellara, both married an **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, and there is **one** Chiara Rivetti death in fifty years of registers, «*vedova di PASQUALE FALCO*».

**NOTHING IS MERGED.** What would settle it: **Michele/Michelangelo's own death act** — he was alive 7 February 1862 and is in no Arienzo register to 1865, **so he died after the series ends**; or the **1808 baptism read from the image**, which names the father and sits behind row 18.

**AND ONE LEAF IS OWED.** Raffaela Falco's death act of 20 April 1854 (`an_ua14356`) is a **citation in this archive's register and has never been re-read at full resolution**. It should be — it is now load-bearing, and today's whole lesson is that a swept or cited row becomes evidence the moment something is built on it.

rows.what: The married-in page cannot see the people documented only from acts
rows.note:
**Raised 22 September 2026, out of an audit of whether the site had kept up with the research.**

`tools/build_marriedin.py` builds **from the MyHeritage tree** and joins to this archive on the tree's own id — correctly, because **103 of the 294 people on that page share a name with somebody else on it**, so a name join would point a third of the links at a guess.

**The consequence is that a person documented only from an act is not on the page at all.** **Twelve of the thirteen people this archive marks «married in» are missing**, among them **ANGELA CARFORA**, who married Giuseppe Falco in December 1854 and whose whole filiation is read from the act; **VINCENZO ABATIELLO**, who married Angela Falco in 1865; **CORNELIA SABATINO**, who married Francesco Falco in 1854; and **FILOMENA DI LUCIA**, who married Stanislao Falco in 1861.

**What was fixed on the day, and what was not.** Where the tree is blank and the archive is not, the build now uses **the archive's own dates** — twelve fields, four births and eight deaths. **Mariantonia Carfora** had no date span on that page while her birth act of 30 December 1830 and her marriage act of 21 January 1860 were both published and both cited on her own person page. *That fixed the dates of the people who are on the page; it did not put the missing ones on it.*

**Why it was not done in the same pass.** Every surname on that page carries a **reach** — whether it carries Falco blood, married one, is such a family, or married into one of those — and that is computed by walking the **tree's** topology. A person with no tree row has no topology to walk, so admitting them means deciding what «reach» means for somebody the tree has never heard of. **That is a design question, not a patch**, and the page now states the gap in its own words rather than hiding it.

**The honest interim.** The page says how many it cannot see, and the number is **derived from the household file**, so it cannot drift away from the truth while nobody is looking — which is the failure this whole audit was about.

rows.what: The Arienzo death registers 1813, 1814 and 1815 — the last three of the decade

**CLOSED 22 September 2026. All seven volumes of 1809–1815 are read out on BOTH halves.** 1813, 1814 and 1815 were read the same day: they gave **six Falco women married into other Arienzo houses**, **a son of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida** who was not in this archive, **Giuseppe Falco's own stated age**, and **two siblings for Antonia di Guida** with both their parents named.

rows.what: Re-prove the layout of every register volume ever swept by a half-page band
rows.note:
**Raised 22 September 2026, out of the discovery that two volumes published as «read in full» were half read.**

A band sweep of one half of each image reads half the acts **consistently**, so the output looks like a complete sweep and nothing appears to be missing. In 1809 and 1811 **both Falco acts that had already been found happened to sit on right pages**, so the method confirmed itself. The unread halves held **four more Falco**, one of them a couple a generation above this archive's head of line.

**The check is cheap:** render one full page, read the act number on each half, and compare image *n*'s left-page number with image *n+1*'s. **If they differ by two, there are two acts per image.**

**What this row is for:** every volume in `notes/` whose progress file records a `--half L` or `--half R` band needs that check run against it, and its coverage row amended or confirmed. **Until then, every nil published from a half-page sweep is only as good as its volume's layout.** [[wrong-negatives]]

rows.what: A household's identity is its NAME, and that is why four of them could be duplicated invisibly
rows.note:
**Raised 23 September 2026, after four household names were published twice in one night with every gate green.** A gate now catches it — `tools/check_households.py` — **but the gate treats a symptom.**

**The diagnosis came from the session that maintains the shared kit**, which ran the question across every archive in the estate that holds a households file:

| archive | households | identity |
|---|---|---|
| D'Arcy | 199 | the couple — *(a, b, married, place)* |
| Defranceski | 127 | `key` / `id` |
| Mazza | 276 | `headId` |
| **this archive** | **111** | **`name`** |

**Three of the four cannot have this bug**, not because their scripts are more careful but because appending a duplicate would create a visibly duplicate id. **Mazza has five households whose NAMES repeat** — «Orazio Mazza» twice, «Maria Mazza» three times — **and none whose `headId` repeats**: five genuinely distinct people, held apart correctly, by an archive whose rule is that it never merges on a name.

**This archive merges households on a name while refusing to merge people on one.** `H.append({...})` without a lookup, and `by.pop(name)` leaving the list entry behind, are both only possible because the index is keyed on a display string.

**WHAT A FIX WOULD LOOK LIKE, AND WHY IT IS NOT DONE HERE.** **756 of 757 member rows already carry an `ark`.** A household keyed on its father's and mother's arks, with the name kept as a label, would make the duplicate check *structural* rather than a gate, and would close the second check too — a member's back-reference would point at an id instead of a string that has to match character for character.

**It is a change to the shape of this archive's central file**, touching 111 households, 757 rows, five builders and `households.tsv`. **That is David's call, not a patch to make at the end of an unattended session.** The gate holds the line until then.

**DONE 23 September 2026, on David's own ruling in this session** — and **not on the shape that was proposed**, because that shape is not available.

**THE ARK-PAIR KEY CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DATA.** «756 of 757 member rows carry an ark» is true and does not translate: a household key needs the father's ark and the mother's ark to be **different**, and **75 of 111 households cannot supply two distinct parent arks**. The commonest reason is not a gap — it is the archive working correctly. **A couple named together in one act share ONE ark, because they are one document**: «*Nicola Rivetti & Anna di Ruggio*» are both `an_ua14345 img30r atto43`. And **eleven households are a single person with no spouse at all** — «*Tommaso Zampiello*», «*Gioacchino Falco (strada Camellara)*».

**WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD: a frozen assigned id.** Every household carries `id`; every member carries `hid`; `data/households.tsv` carries an **hid column**; `build_people.py` keys people on `id` instead of on the display string; `check_households.py` fails on a missing or duplicated id and on a member whose `hid` does not match its house; and `check_release.py` matches the two household files **on the id** rather than the name.

**THE NAME IS STILL PARSED, AND THAT IS CORRECT.** «X & Y» is this archive's statement of who the parents are — it is *data*. What it is no longer is *identity*.

**THE REKEY MOVED NOTHING.** Zero person slugs changed, zero relationship edges changed, zero records changed household. A rekey that alters behaviour is a rekey that was doing something else.

**WHAT IT BUYS, IN ONE EXAMPLE.** `check_release.py` has carried a hand-written rename table — `{"Francesco Cossi & Maria Falco": "Francesco Cioffi & Maria Falco"}` — purely because a household was corrected in one file and not the other, and the gate would otherwise fail on the archive's own correction. **With an id, a rename is one field and that table is dead weight.** The «Michele Crisci → Nicola Crisci» correction that produced a duplicate household on 22 September could not have done so.

**AND THE NEW CHECK HAD THE NIGHT'S OWN FAULT IN ITS FIRST DRAFT**: the id-resolution test in `check_release.py` printed «FAILED» and **exited zero**, because it set a flag no other line read. *A gate that reports and does not refuse is the same thing as no gate.* Fixed and tested by injecting an unresolvable hid.

rows.what: TWO ANGELA MARIA FALCO ARE ON ONE PAGE, fifty years and two sets of parents apart
rows.note:
**Found 23 September 2026 by a date check, not by a name check** — which is the only reason it was found at all.

`/people/angela-maria-falco/` currently carries **four parents**:

- **from the registers** — a daughter of **GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA**, born **19 January 1822** by an act that names her grandfather, married **15 November 1857**;
- **from the family tree** (id 4512504) — born **1772**, died **14 September 1850**, daughter of **FRANCESCO FALCO and MADDALENA SICILIATTO**.

**Fifty years, different parents, one page.** They were joined on «**name alone**», which is the weakest basis `build_people.py` accepts and — by construction — **the basis it uses precisely when the years do NOT agree**: `best == 0` means the two sides' years failed to overlap, and the merge proceeds anyway if each side has exactly one candidate.

**A GUARD WAS WRITTEN AND WITHDRAWN THE SAME HOUR.** Refusing «name alone» wherever the years failed to overlap cost **ten** merges to fix this **one**, and nine of the ten were correct: **Alessandra Crisci** has a tree birth of **1817** and a register marriage of **1834** — *years that do not overlap and do not contradict either, because a birth year and a marriage year never overlap.* **Absence of agreement is not disagreement, and the first version of the rule could not tell them apart.**

**What a correct guard needs** is to compare like with like — the household's BIRTH event against the tree's `b`, its DEATH event against the tree's `d` — and to refuse only when one of those pairs both exists and disagrees. *That is a careful piece of work on the archive's central builder and it was not done at the end of an unattended night.*

**Until then the build prints the conflict on every run** — «*ACTS THAT CONTRADICT A TREE DATE — the act is used, the MERGE is suspect*» — so it cannot go quiet. **The act's date is what the page shows**, on the archive's own ranking of line over register over tree.

**The likely answer is that the tree's 1772 woman is not this archive's at all**: a Francesco Falco and a Maddalena Siciliatto appear nowhere in the registers read so far. **Unmerging is probably right, and proving it is the work.** [[two-falco-families-arienzo]]

**DONE 23 September 2026, on David's own ruling in this session: unmerge AND fix the rule.**

**The proof:** every Siciliatto row in this archive is sourced «*the family tree (unverified unless a record is cited)*» — **none in `households.tsv`, none in the notes** — and the tree gives Francesco Falco's own parents as «*[Unconfirmed Family] Falco*». **The 1772 woman rests on nothing this archive has read.** She keeps a tree-only page, because an unverified person is not a deleted one.

**The rule now compares like with like** and refuses exactly one merge, with its reason printed: «*angela maria falco — birth [1822] vs tree [1772]*». **The fourteen other «name alone» merges stand**, including Alessandra Crisci, whose 1817 birth and 1834 marriage the first attempt wrongly called a contradiction.
